Res. 73)
bill.status: Introduced in Senate · Whitehouse · referred to Environment and Public Works
bill.analyzed: Full introduced joint resolution (two pages; one operative clause)

provisions.title: S.J. Res. 73
provisions.heading: Congressional disapproval of the identified EPA aerosol-coatings interim final rule
provisions.quote: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to National Volatile Organic Compound Emission Standards for Aerosol Coatings: Interim Final Rule (90 Fed. Reg. 28904 (July 2, 2025)), and such rule shall have no force or effect.
provisions.context:
S.J. Res. 73 invokes chapter 8 of title 5 and identifies one EPA interim final rule by title and Federal Register citation. Mr. Whitehouse introduced it on August 1, 2025; it was read twice and referred to the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works. Its sole operative clause states that Congress disapproves the cited rule and that the rule shall have no force or effect. Because the supplied version is introduced text, that consequence is contingent on enactment.

Source limits / honesty note: The supplied flattened text identifies the rule but does not reproduce it, state its requirements, articulate findings or a purpose beyond disapproval, specify implementation steps, or identify a quantitative outcome. The matching official PDF establishes pagination at two pages, but the flat extraction omits page boundaries and the standard resolving formula. This analysis therefore records only the express legal objective and enactment-contingent effect. It makes no claims about emissions, public health, compliance costs, aerosol-coating production, regulated entities, or the post-disapproval regulatory baseline. It has zero forecastable metrics, series hints, stance matrices, or empirical conditionals.
goals: Disapprove the identified EPA interim final rule so that it has no force or effect.

effects.mechanism: Direct legal effect — conditional on enactment
effects.text: If enacted, the resolution would disapprove the EPA rule cited at 90 Fed. Reg. 28904 and provide that the rule has no force or effect.
